author: Trash Theory
description:
The Human League were revolutionary. Taking the anyone can play guitar sentiment of punk and applying it to a newly affordable array of synthesisers, in the late seventies the band pioneered the idea of fully electronic-pop in Britain, like a Yorkshire version of Kraftwerk. But then half the band left and the remaining members, their singer and slide projectionist, managed to pick up the pieces and conquer the world, with a focus on image that foresaw the future of pop. Their fourth single from 1981’s Dare was half cheesy synth-duet half vicious dissection of male ego, and arguably the first international synth-pop mega hit. And the band couldn’t stand it. This is New British Canon, and this is the story of “Don’t You Want Me”.

#thehumanleague  #synthpop  #musicdocumentary 

Fact-checking by Chad Van Wagner.
